svg.text: A reversible reel-to-reel mat is conveyor, work surface, mixing trough, rolling mat and chute — and washes itself on the way back.
bay 900 W × 600 D × 650 H (+150 mat magazine)
13 actuators, all rotary shafts through the back wall
mat 440 wide × ~1.4 m, glass-fabric silicone 1 mm
mat wash 3–4 L · 3–4 min, A0 > 60 by steam
FRONT VIEW, 1 px per mm (everything is uniform into the page, 440 mm)
fixed tool rail under a drip hood (tools on back-wall shafts)

g.text: log Ø60 laid back on the table

svg.text: cold pre-rinse + scraper on the edge roller
55 °C detergent spray from both sides (8 flat fans)
steam bar: 1 mm mat > 90 °C in 5 s → A0 > 60

g.text: SHUTTLE
wind on A or B; food passes under a fixed tool
LOOP
B swings in: slack loop = drum with a soft wall
NIP
roller presses on the table, gap 0–60, ≤ 600 N
CHOP
blade against the mat while the mat jogs
NOSE
B swings out and down: mat pulled from under the food
Peel, don't pull: a flexible mat is peeled off sticky
food by force per width, not per area.
Each mat after each use: reeled B → A and back through the sink.
Every cm² passes a nozzle at 40 mm: no spray shadow by construction.
Steam slot 100 mm at 20 mm/s: 5 s, > 90 °C (mat is 1 mm thin).
Heat 0.6 kg mat by 80 K: ~60 kJ, ~25 g steam.
3–4 L and 3–4 min per mat, against 17–20 L and 1 h per chamber load.
Mats (hem rods snap onto magnets in the bars):
M1 glass-fabric silicone: dough, mince, breading
M2 TPU belt: cutting anvil, raw meat, carving
M3 perforated: wash, drain, steam
M4 mesh belt: mangle ricer
M5 rasp sheet: abrasive peeling
M6 moulded cavities: patties, dumplings
Fixed parts (table, cheeks, roller, blade, 0.45 m²) washed in place;
dies, bowl, tips go to the wash chamber. Mats: yearly wear part.
Weak point: mat life (blade, steam, onion oil); sticky dough.

svg.text: 1/8 SHUTTLE: box tips mince onto the mat; the mat carries it under the pipette (egg)
2/8 LOOP: bar B swings in, the slack mat hangs as a trough; winding tumbles the mass
3/8 NIP: the mass is drawn under the roller and pressed flat — LOOP + NIP cycles knead and mix
4/8 In the loop the mass rolls up on itself into a Ø60 log
5/8 CHOP: log back on the table; the blade cuts 30 mm pucks while the mat jogs
6/8 NOSE: B swings out and down and winds in — the mat slides out from under the pucks into the pan
7/8 WASH: the mat runs through the sink — pre-rinse, hot spray both sides, rinse, steam, air knife
8/8 Clean dry mat, back to the start: ~4 L and 3–4 min
